sentiment.label: Mixed
sentiment.summary: Coverage this hour centres on very heavy trading volume and a weak broader market, with shares reported well below the morning high but still above the $83 IPO price. I could not confirm a fresh price from two sources, so the read rests on commentary and the last confirmed levels.
points: CNBC reports volume above 640 million shares by mid-session, more than SpaceX's debut-day total
Last reported levels were about $96 at 12:20pm ET (Fox News) and about $101 at 12:31pm ET (MLQ, citing Nasdaq), versus the $111.50 open and $83 IPO price
Fox News notes the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq were each down more than 1% in the afternoon
Melius Research initiated with a Buy and $155 target, per CNBC, while the WSJ editorial board has called valuations stretched

updates.text: CNBC reports that ANT's volume had passed 640 million shares by mid-session, more than SpaceX's 522 million on its debut day, making it the most actively traded stock on Nasdaq.
CNBC says Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley stand to earn roughly $550 million in fees from the offering, above the roughly $500 million banks earned on SpaceX's IPO.
Fox News notes that the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq Composite were each down more than 1% in the afternoon, and that underwriters have until 18 December to buy 147 million extra shares at $83.

CNBC's live blog says Melius Research has started coverage of Anthropic with a Buy rating and a $155 price target. It also reports that roughly half of institutional investors who placed orders received no allocation in the offering.

Shares slipped from an intraday high of $114.99 to about $101 by 12:31pm ET, according to MLQ, citing Nasdaq data. Around 484 million shares had changed hands, roughly half the number sold in the offering.

Anthropic's Class A shares began trading on Nasdaq at about 11:48am ET, opening at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price. The stock debuted well over two hours after the opening bell, valuing the company at roughly $2 trillion.

Anthropic filed its final prospectus with the SEC on the morning of 19 November, confirming 980 million Class A shares at $83 (about $81.3bn). The sale is expected to close on 20 November, with a separate $26bn Class N share sale to seven tech companies to follow and a 30-day option for banks to buy up to 147 million more shares.

Khaleej Times reports that Anthropic is expected to join at least six major indexes, including the Nasdaq 100, within 5 to 15 days of listing, and that a separate $26 billion private sale with cornerstone investors is also planned.

Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range, selling 980 million shares and raising $81.3 billion. Trading on Nasdaq under ANT is expected from 9:30am New York time on 19 November.
